page: Microsoft Azure D4ls_v5 is a general purpose, low-memory virtual machine instance hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The architecture incorporates 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, along with hardware extensions such as AVX-512, VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic accelerators. System memory totals 8.0 GB, allocating 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The hardware configuration omits local disk storage entirely, requiring network-attached storage for operating system and application persistent data. Similarly, it features no dedicated hardware accelerators, providing zero GPUs. The 1:2 ratio of vCPUs to memory designates this instance as a low-memory variant within the D-series family, minimizing memory footprint overhead for workloads where extensive volatile capacity is unneeded.

Benchmark results demonstrate intermediate single-thread throughput alongside constrained multi-core and memory subsystem capabilities. The instance achieved average results in single-core stress-ng (1897.19) and Geekbench single-core testing (1651.0), with static web serving reaching 6.49 GB/sec. However, parallel execution results sit in the bottom quartiles, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 3513.0 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression of 19.81 GB/sec. Memory subsystem evaluation showed a PassMark memory score of 924.87 and small-block cached read bandwidth of 209.52 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom percentiles.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the reduced memory footprint provides a qualitative economic advantage over standard 1:4 memory instances when application memory requirements are minimal. The primary tradeoff lies in the lack of local temporary storage and diminished parallel scaling. The instance is suited for lightweight web serving, stateless microservices, routine batch processing, and non-memory-intensive containerized workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D4ls_v5 is an entry-tier general purpose instance configured with a low-memory ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz, it provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system includes 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding 2.0 GB per vCPU, and integrates AVX-512 vector acceleration. The instance does not include integrated local SSD storage or GPU acceleration, depending entirely on remote storage arrays. Benchmark indicators display standard baseline performance in single-threaded operations, including static web serving and cryptographic tasks, but demonstrate reduced capacity under multi-threaded processing and memory-intensive evaluations. The reduced memory ratio provides an efficient hardware footprint for compute-oriented tasks that do not demand large RAM volumes, making it suitable for lightweight microservices, basic web application hosting, build agents, and stateless API endpoints.
